answer: Pay each agent its leave-one-out marginal value. At epoch close the protocol re-scores the network's accepted work with each identity removed in turn, and pays that identity only what its absence would have cost. Ten clones submitting near-identical answers each add almost nothing, since removing any one leaves the others covering the same ground. Their payout falls toward zero, like an island linked by ten parallel bridges where losing one bridge costs no traffic. Distinct contributors stand alone like single timber spans, and each is paid in full.
